#1629. England given 10% chance of Spain Nations League win as Ben White/Cole Palmer claim made

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 10:43

Ahead of Sunday's UEFA Nations League battle between Spain and England, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton explains why the Three Lions only have a "10-15%" chance of topping the group and makes an intriguing claim over Ben White and Cole Palmer.

I'd give them a very slim chance. We know that any win will do because in the Nations League, head-to-head results take precedence over goal difference.

If England win by one goal, they're level with Spain on head-to-head points, head-to-head goal difference and head-to-head goals scored, so then overall goal difference takes precedence, where England are superior to Spain.

If they win by two or three goals, then they top the group as well.

It's quite hard to judge based on what we've seen in one game, especially because I think we're now at that point in the season where fatigue is building and domestic and European commitments are really ramping up, especially for Premier League players.

I think we saw a bit of that in England's performance against Croatia. Quite a few standout names, I wouldn't say they had off nights, but they were just OK.

Lewis Hall was a standout, and Morgan Rogers too, but there was no one I really thought, "Wow, that was a magnificent individual display."

A win against Croatia is still nothing really to be scoffed at, even if they're not the Croatia side that they used to be. But facing world champions Spain, it's not impossible, of course. Nothing is impossible in football, but it'd be a very slim chance for me.

There is one thing that England are better at than Spain recently; they've scored two or more goals in each of their last six games, while Spain have done it in each of their last five.

Although the last time Spain scored just the one goal was in the World Cup final, so I can't really get too big-headed on that front.

Spain are now unbeaten in 43 matches, they haven't lost in 32 months, so I'd be pretty shocked if England could get the job done.

It's going to be really interesting to see what Tuchel does team news wise, because we're hoping that he'll be boosted by as many as three returns for this game.

Lewis-Skelly was banned against Croatia, and he'll return here. Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence just trained individually before the Croatia game, but there's hope that they'll return. I would absolutely start Konsa over Quansah for this game.

It's going to be fascinating to see whether Ben White comes in at right-back. He was booed again last night when he came off the bench.

He previously came out and said that if people knew the full story, then they wouldn't boo him. Now I'm just thinking, if Cole Palmer comes back into the squad, is he going to get the same level of treatment?

It is not an identical situation to Ben White, pulling out for load management versus personal reasons, but that's one I'll be fascinated to see if he gets called up in March.

Interestingly, I have seen some criticism of Declan Rice in an England kit. With Arsenal, Arteta really plays to his strengths, dropping him in between the centre-backs, where he can play those line-breaking passes.

We don't really see that so often for England, so I've seen quite a few people saying if Alex Scott was in the squad, they would start him alongside Elliot Anderson.

Lewis-Skelly is another option now that he's back from his ban, but I think it'll be Rice and Anderson in the middle. It'll be the same front four, but I would give them maybe a 10 to 15% chance of getting the win they need to top the group.

#1627. Harry Kane is annoyed at his '50-50' England team-mates who pull out of international duty, reveals Thomas Tuchel

Published: 14:15 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 16:29 EST, 11 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Harry Kane is annoyed by team-mates who pull out of England squads – and says his captain would never do so.

Several of the head coach’s camps have been blighted by withdrawals, including Cole Palmer’s ‘load management’ excuse in September. The Chelsea playmaker was then left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League fixtures.

And Tuchel says Kane, who will become England’s record cap-holder with his 126th appearance against Croatia on Thursday evening, is not a fan of those who pass up the opportunity to play for their country.

‘He is always here and doesn’t like it if 50-50 decisions are taken by the players not to come to camp,’ said Tuchel.

‘We had this conversation very early when I took the job and it was one of his points, to make sure that players come and are proud to arrive because it’s the biggest honour.

‘We need to make sure that if it happens (withdrawals) we are so strong that we actually set the tone that everybody is desperate to be in camp, because everybody can lose their shirt if they miss out on a camp.

Thomas Tuchel (centre) has revealed Harry Kane's frustrations at his team-mates pulling out the England squad

Cole Palmer (right), pictured with Kane in 2024, has been criticised by Tuchel for missing too many England opportunities

‘So it was one of the first discussions and straight away he set the standard and made it very clear where the standards are for him. He would never pull out. Never.’

Kane, meanwhile, says his desire burns brighter than ever as he targets 100 England goals and records that will stand for generations.

He insists he is far from finished and has warned team-mates Declan Rice and Jude Bellingham that his caps record could yet reach 150.

‘This is no time to rest,’ said Kane. ‘I've got better year on year. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘Jude and Dec, they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are. So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! Before we know it, it’ll be the home Euros. I might be on 140 caps by then, and then we'll be talking about 150. My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I have an ego to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

#1626. Jorge Jesus responds after Cristiano Ronaldo tribute ends in Portugal record defeat

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 10:52

Portugal's first home match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement was supposed to celebrate the end of an extraordinary era. Instead, a 4-1 defeat to Denmark produced the country's heaviest-ever home loss in competitive football and prompted a remarkably blunt response from Jorge Jesus about his former captain.

The Portuguese players walked onto the pitch in Braga wearing Ronaldo's iconic number seven shirt, while supporters unveiled a giant banner reading "Obrigado, Capitão" — "Thank you, Captain".

An additional tribute followed in the seventh minute, with Ronaldo's image appearing on the stadium screens as fans applauded the 41-year-old, who announced his international retirement on November 5.

By the final whistle, however, the atmosphere had changed dramatically. Some supporters had left the stadium, while others chanted Ronaldo's name as Denmark inflicted a humiliating defeat on the reigning Nations League champions.

Asked afterwards whether Portugal were missing their former captain, Jesus delivered a pointed response.

"How can I miss him when he's no longer with the national team? What is there to miss? Maybe just his company," the 72-year-old told reporters.

"He doesn't play anymore, he's not here and he's already decided his future."

The comments added another chapter to the strained relationship between Ronaldo and Jesus, whose disagreement over the forward's international role preceded his retirement.

The scale of Saturday's defeat becomes even more striking when placed alongside Portugal's history.

According to Portuguese statistics outlet Zerozero, the national team had never previously lost a competitive home fixture by three goals or more.

Portugal's last defeat by such a margin on home soil came on September 6, 2003, when Spain secured a 3-0 friendly victory in Guimaraes.

Ronaldo had made his senior international debut against Kazakhstan just 17 days earlier, at the age of 18.

It means Portugal's first home match following his retirement produced a result not seen on Portuguese soil since the opening weeks of his international career.

The last time Portugal had lost 4-1 at home was even earlier, against Finland in a friendly on March 27, 2002.

There is an important distinction: those previous defeats came in friendlies, whereas Denmark's victory was achieved in a competitive Nations League fixture.

The timing was particularly painful given the elaborate tribute organised by the Portuguese Football Federation to recognise Ronaldo's 23 years of international service.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward ended his international career with 146 goals in 234 appearances, leaving behind records that underline the significance of his departure.

Saturday's celebrations were intended to recognise those achievements, but the match also exposed problems that Portugal must address without their former captain.

Rasmus Hojlund, another former Manchester United forward, scored twice for Denmark, while Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and Joachim Andersen were also on target.

Bernardo Silva's stoppage-time goal merely reduced the margin of defeat.

Portugal had won their previous four Nations League matches under Jesus, including a 4-2 victory over Denmark in Copenhagen on October 1.

Six weeks later, the same opponents exposed serious weaknesses in the Portuguese defensive organisation.

Jesus refused to connect Ronaldo's absence directly with Saturday's result, insisting that the former captain had already made his decision regarding international football.

The Portuguese manager nevertheless acknowledged the significance of Ronaldo's contribution and understood why supporters were chanting his name.

He explained that fans would naturally remember everything Ronaldo had achieved over 23 years with the national team, while recognising that some had left the stadium because of their disappointment with the scoreline.

On the pitch, Jesus identified a more immediate explanation for the collapse.

Speaking at his post-match press conference, as reported by A Bola, the former Benfica manager admitted that his side had been unable to contain Denmark's attacking movements, particularly after half-time.

He pointed to failures throughout Portugal's defensive structure rather than blaming the back four alone.

The pressing, usually a defining feature of his teams, had been especially ineffective.

Jesus acknowledged that Portugal's players repeatedly arrived too late to challenge the Danish ball-carrier, allowing the visitors to move possession forward before pressure could be applied.

That failure left the defensive line exposed, with Denmark exploiting spaces between Portugal's defenders.

The manager also admitted that the result had forced him to reconsider his plans for Tuesday's final group fixture against Wales.

He had initially intended to give opportunities to several players in Cardiff, but Saturday's performance means he may now rely more heavily on those who helped Portugal win their opening four matches.

Despite the historic nature of the defeat, Jesus rejected the suggestion that his previous work should be called into question.

He reminded his players that Portugal remained top of Nations League Group A4 and still controlled their own position.

The Portuguese have 12 points, three more than Denmark, and have already secured their place in the quarter-finals.

However, the Danes now hold the head-to-head advantage following Saturday's result and could overtake Portugal if they defeat Norway and Jesus's side lose to Wales.

A draw in Cardiff would be enough for Portugal to finish first.

Jesus therefore faces an immediate challenge: restoring the defensive discipline that disappeared against Denmark while preparing a team beginning life without its most influential international figure.

The Ronaldo tributes were meant to mark the end of one chapter in Portuguese football. Saturday's result has ensured that the beginning of the next will face considerable scrutiny.

However, despite losing four of their five matches, Wales are in a strong position to secure a relegation playoff tie in March.

Meanwhile, Portugal travel to Cardiff on the back of a surprise 4-1 defeat at home to Denmark on Saturday.

After Cristiano Ronaldo's recent international retirement, Jorge Jesus would have been hoping for a fifth win in succession, but he and his players were given a reality check having fallen four goals behind come the 75th minute.

Although they have already secured a spot in the quarter-finals, Portugal must avoid defeat to leave Denmark unable to overtake them for first place on the final matchday.

The only clean sheet of Jesus's reign so far was in the 1-0 victory over Wales on matchday one.

With Ethan Ampadu serving a suspension, Josh Sheehan could be drafted into the Wales midfield.

Connor Roberts is expected to replace the injured Neco Williams at right-back, while Bellamy may try to find a role for David Brooks after his goal in Norway.

Meanwhile, Antonio Silva is in line to deputise for Ruben Dias in the Portugal defence, a consequence of the Manchester City centre-back serving a suspension.

#1621. Pep Guardiola 'set to be made top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as United States boss' as ex-Spurs manager closes in on Man United job

Published: 16:04 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:13 EST, 11 November 2026

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola will be the United States' top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino if and when their manager joins Manchester United, according to a report.

It is looking more and more likely that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will take over from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford in the coming days.

Pochettino is currently with his United States Men's National Team players ahead of their fixtures against Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League this fortnight, but is expected to join up with United after those games.

That will leave the United States needing a new boss and, according to The Athletic, they will set their sights on Guardiola.

The Spaniard is renowned as one of the best managers around, having won the Champions League and six Premier League titles while with City.

He also has historic success with Bayern Munich and Barcelona, and has previously shown interest in potentially moving into international football.

The United States are reportedly set to make Pep Guardiola (pictured) their top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as manager

Pochettino (right) is set to leave his role at the USMNT to take over at Manchester United

As recently as the summer, Guardiola  came so close to being appointed Italy manager that he was 'writing down line-ups' before ultimately deciding not to take the role on.

He was touted to take over an under-performing Italian national team, but the move fell through, and Italian Football Federation technical director and defensive legend Paolo Maldini resigned after a move to appoint Andrea Pirlo also collapsed due to his commercial links with a Russian betting company.

Maldini opened up on how close Guardiola came to taking over the team, revealing that the Spaniard was seemingly on board for a pretty long time.

'(Guardiola) is the coach who best embodies technical, attacking football,' Maldini told Corriere della Sera. 'He had expressed the idea of wanting to coach a national team to some friends.

'We went to meet him in Barcelona, we had lunch together, we talked for an entire day.

'He was very tempted. He came very close to accepting. He even started writing line-ups down on sheets of paper.'

It is reported that Guardiola has spoken to officials at the US national side in the past and is intrigued by working in America. He lived in New York briefly after leaving Barcelona in 2012.

He is said to have been approached in 2024 before Pochettino was appointed, and wished the Argentine well upon his appointment.

Pochettino is currently away with the States but is likely to join United in the coming days

He said: 'I wish him and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager.'

He has also been previously quoted as saying: 'The USA is fascinating to try and build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step. The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on.'

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were in Monaco where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick's departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino's appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday.

#1620. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

#1618. Republic of Ireland vs Kosovo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 15 Nov 2026 11:44

Facing off for a UEFA Nations League playoff spot, the Republic of Ireland and Kosovo will clash at Dublin's Aviva Stadium on Tuesday night.

With the hosts trailing their visitors by one point in League B Group 3, the pair are vying for second place behind confirmed winners Austria.

Any hope of securing automatic promotion to Europe's top level was ended when Ireland lost in Austria on Saturday night, leaving them six points adrift of their hosts.

Ending the stubborn resistance of goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher, who produced a string of sharp saves throughout the match, substitute Sasa Kalajdzic notched a late winner in Linz.

As a result, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side sit third in Group 3, one point behind Kosovo, who they must now beat on the final matchday.

The stakes are quite high, as victory would ensure both a Nations League promotion playoff and entry to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

At the outset, Hallgrimsson highlighted how positive results in this campaign would aid Ireland's aim of reaching a Euros that will be partly played on home soil.

Another set of circumstances could instead send them into a relegation playoff against League C opponents - if they lose again and Israel defeat Austria, the Boys in Green will finish fourth.

Yet, having kicked off with a 1-0 loss in Pristina earlier this season, Ireland will welcome Kosovo to Dublin with an historic promotion still up for grabs.

After both sides endured agony in the World Cup playoffs, Kosovo came out on top in September's Group 3 opener, as Vedat Muriqi finally broke through with a late winner.

Franco Foda's team have made rapid progress in the Nations League, previously finishing second in their League C section, before winning both legs of a playoff against Iceland.

Now in Europe's second tier for the first time, Kosovo could soon ascend straight up to League A.

If they avoid defeat on Tuesday evening, the Balkan nation will guarantee entry to the promotion playoffs, which are set to take place in March.

Second spot would have been even more firmly within their grasp but for failing to beat Israel last time out, when Veldin Hodza was sent off in a 0-0 home draw.

Even so, having picked up a single point from three consecutive fixtures, one more will be enough to keep Kosovo's campaign alive.

Despite Ireland's loss in Linz, Hallgrimsson is likely to keep a settled side, with captain Nathan Collins helming the hosts' defence.

While Collins is back after missing the first four Nations League matches through injury, Burnley midfielder Josh Cullen and Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu are not available.

After forming an attacking trident in recent games, Jack Moylan and Adam Idah should continue to support Troy Parrott up front.

The latter may have endured a dry spell with Real Betis, but he has scored 10 goals in his last eight competitive appearances for Ireland.

Meanwhile, Muriqi is set to spearhead Kosovo's front line, as their captain and all-time top scorer with 33 international goals - including one in the reverse fixture.

Como winger Mergim Vojvoda should feature in Muriqi's supporting cast, but Juventus forward Edon Zhegrova has just withdrawn due to injury.

Ermal Krasniqi and Lumbardh Dellova - both of Turkish Super Lig surprise package Amedspor - were already ruled out, while Hodza must serve a suspension.

Republic of Ireland possible starting lineup:

Kelleher; O'Shea, Collins, Scales; Abankwah, Molumby, Azaz, Manning; Moylan; Idah, Parrott

Saipi; Kamberi, I. Krasniqi, Raci, Gallapeni; Emerllahu, Avdullahu; Vojvoda, Rashica, Zabergja; Muriqi

September's loss in Pristina was one of only two in Ireland's last 13 matches, and the Boys in Green generally raise their game on home turf.

As Kosovo are missing some key men from a thin squad, they may suffer defeat in Dublin and slip down to third place.

#1616. Ryan Porteous reckons people are still reading too much into THAT red card against Germany that made him a pariah with Tartan Army

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EST, 11 November 2026

From a distance, it was difficult not to look at the fall-out from Ryan Porteous’ rash challenge on Ilkay Gundogan in the opening match of Euro 2024 and draw sweeping conclusions.

Coming on the cusp of half-time in the Allianz Arena, the defender’s two-footed lunge on the German midfielder earned him a straight red card with a two-game suspension soon following.

The moment of madness led to Kai Havertz giving the host nation a three-goal lead from the penalty spot at the interval. By time-up, Steve Clarke’s depleted side had lost 5-1. The self-belief which they’d brought into the tournament was fast evaporating, too.

While no one doubted the scale of the task Scotland faced before a ball was kicked that evening, Porteous’ actions made the mission impossible. As a consequence, the former Hibernian defender found forgiveness hard to come by.

Those irate Scotland supporters who demanded that he suffered for his folly were granted their wish.

A player who’d featured in seven of the eight qualifiers disappeared from view thereafter, briefly emerging from international exile as a sub against Greece in March of last year, yet posted missing again throughout the World Cup qualifiers and from the tournament itself.

Ryan Porteous' red card gave Scotland a mountain to climb in Euro 2024 defeat to Germany

It seemed only logical to deduce that Clarke had also shared the anger of the Tartan Army and that the player’s status as a pariah was down to his simmering fury at the humiliation that woeful tackle caused.

Porteous always believed the matter wasn’t quite as clear cut as most imagine it to be.

‘I think people maybe read too much into that,’ said the 27-year-old.

‘In the conversations I had with Steve after the Euros and in the next qualifying campaign, the red card against Germany never came up.

‘We had loads of conversations, both when I was in and out of the squad.

‘Those are the things that people obviously don’t see.

‘They maybe think Steve Clarke is the type of person who wouldn’t phone you or text you. But he did. We spoke loads to be honest. He was really honest with me.

‘I texted him when he left the role and he messaged back eager to see me get back in the squad.

The Scotland defender was shown a straight red for this challenge on Ilkay Gundogan

‘Everyone knows Steve is a manager who, if he picks a squad and they do well for them and they get to a tournament, he’s loyal.

‘In terms of the conversations we had during those latter stages of qualification, he just told me to keep doing what I was doing.

‘He was honest and told me I would probably need some of those lads to drop off in form if I was going to make it. You have to respect that.

‘I went to a tournament in the Euros in 2024 and you had someone like John Souttar who missed out. So, I know what it feels like on both sides.’

Porteous, to his credit, doesn’t appear to be bitter about how matters unfolded post-Germany.

Regardless of the true importance of the red card in his status changing from mainstay to that of an outcast, he accepts that fairness and the game do not always walk hand-in-hand.

‘That happens in football, it’s just one of those things,’ he shrugged.

‘I’ve had a career where I’m up and down, I’m left and right, you just need to bounce back from it.

‘It was a fantastic experience for me to be part of that run we went on. It helped me grow massively. I don’t look at it as being unfair.’

Porteous has now returned from period in wilderness ahead of North Macedonia clash

By the time he’d moved from Watford to Los Angeles to sign for LAFC last August, he’d already reconciled himself with the fact that his Scotland career was in cold storage. The consolation was that this afforded him a different perspective on the November night when history was made.

‘It’s maybe tough when the squads were getting announced and then a couple of days after that,’ he reflected.

‘But then as soon as you’re watching the games, you just become a fan straight away again and want the team to do well.

‘I probably hadn’t experienced that for a while. It was actually good for me watching the World Cup qualifiers - because I was able to sit and watch them straight after training because of the time difference.

‘When Kenny McLean scored from the halfway line (against Denmark) I had half the team in LA shouting and screaming for Scotland! It was brilliant.’

While he’d clearly have preferred to still have been at the heart of things, his new life on the other side of the Atlantic allowed him to sample what it all meant to an invading army in the summer.

‘I had a few days off at one point and I went out to Boston,’ he explained.

‘I didn’t manage to go to the games, but I saw my friends and family who were over and we went to the baseball as well.

‘Being in that fan environment, it just gives you that extra little bit of hunger to get back.’

Porteous in action for Scots at training as they prepare for North Macedonia showdown

The profile of the MLS always offered him that possibility. Porteous’s club counts Gareth Bale and Olivier Giroud among its former players. Son Heung-min is the current star in Tinseltown. The Scot played against - and defeated - Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami in February. In such moments, one can feel a long way from Midlothian.

‘I think I could be the first guy ever to go from Dalkeith to LA! It’s very hot. They are actually choking for a bit of rain just now.

‘I used to blame the East Mains wind for losing my hair, but it’s still falling out over in LA even without the wind.

‘(John) McGinn has already peppered me after seeing a couple of my interviews over there.

‘I’ve had to change my accent so that people can understand me over there.

‘For the first couple of months, everyone was asking me to repeat myself. But it’s an incredible place and I’m enjoying every second.’

LAFC finished sixth in the Western Conference this year, good enough to book a slot in the forthcoming play-offs.

Porteous’ part in that meant he was firmly in Sebastien Pocognoli’s thoughts when Stephen Welsh suffered an untimely injury ahead of the two final Nations League matches.

Over two years on from that hideous night in Munich, this feels like a deserved opportunity to change the narrative which has surrounded him ever since.

‘People pay their money and they can have their opinions on me,’ he said.

‘I’ve got thick skin now. It’s never been an issue for me in terms of managers having to pull me aside and have a word or anything like that.

‘I’m in a good place now. Whatever criticism I get, it only makes me grow stronger as a person.

‘Hopefully, I can come back now a better player than what people saw before.

‘I have still got my strengths and I feel like I’ve added to my game as well from being in different leagues and different environments.’

#1615. Mexico vs Jamaica - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 15 Nov 2026 11:49, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 11:49

Mexico play host to Jamaica in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie on Tuesday night.

Jamaica hold a 3-2 advantage from the opening fixture over the weekend as the Reggae Boys attempt to cause a major surprise in this competition.

With Jamaica having finished second behind Guatemala in their group, Mexico would have been confident of earning an advantage from Saturday's first leg in Kingston.

Instead, Mexico are fortunate to still be competitive in the tie having found themselves 3-0 down by the 63rd minute.

Two goals in the closing 20 minutes kept the World Cup last-16 representatives in the tie, yet Rafael Marquez remains without a win as manager.

The former defender has now overseen two draws and three draws, with El Tri having lost 3-0 and 2-0 to USA and Chile respectively prior to their latest fixture.

As defending champions, it would be a major knock on Marquez should he fail to guide Mexico to at least the last four of the competition.

Meanwhile, Jamaica are attempting to move closer to a second semi-final appearance in three Nations League campaigns.

Having lost out to DR Congo in the World Cup playoffs earlier in the year, Rudolph Speid's side have delivered a strong response.

Although two defeats have been posted in seven games, they defeated El Salvador and earned a draw with Honduras on away territory before Saturday's five-goal thriller.

Jamaica had failed to win their previous six games against Mexico before that contest, emphasising the magnitude of the result.

Kevin Alvarez, Santiago Sandoval, Jesus Corona and Alexis Vega are all in contention for Mexico having helped inspire the comeback during the closing quarter of the first leg.

Despite his role as captain, Cesar Montes could be among those to drop down to the substitutes' bench, along with forward Santiago Gimenez.

Eighteen-year-old Gilberto Mora should keep his spot in a creative midfield role.

As for Jamaica, Denzel Hall may be handed a start over Kyle Ming at right wing-back.

However, Speid could be against making further changes to his side, unless he shows preference towards introducing fresh legs.

Javon East has started the last three games down the middle of the attack.

Waite; Latibeaudiere, Freckleton, King; Hall, Anderson, Clarke, Webster; Dixon, East, Cephas

Despite holding an advantage, we expect Jamaica to try to play their normal game in Guadalupe. However, that may play into the hands of Mexico, who we are backing to qualify for the semi-finals with a decisive late goal.

#1612. Pocognoli fears Scottish Premiership 'identity crisis' over lack of homegrown stars

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:55 EST, 11 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli believes the Premiership has an identity crisis caused by a lack of Scottish players pulling on the jersey at our top clubs.

Just six of the 26 players the newly appointed national team manager initially selected for the Nations League double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland play their football in this country’s top division.

And while the Belgian understands the attraction and the benefits of top talents moving to some of Europe’s top leagues, he’s concerned that the division which should be his first port of call when it comes to making selections is now a barren land.

‘The Scottish league misses Scottish players in the biggest teams,’ he said.

‘The league is intense and competitive, but I am not looking at this. I am looking at who is performing at the big clubs.

‘I believe that’s the most close to international level. And for that you need to play Champions League, Europa League, Conference League in some stage of the competition.

‘That is what I’m looking at. I hope that players who are performing well, let’s say in the bottom (half), can bounce to the next step to a top club inside the country.

Pocognoli has been alarmed by the lack of Scottish talent in the SPFL Premiership

Pocognoli has been impressed by the progress of young Celtic full-back Colby Donovan

‘That will make the competition more competitive, maybe you will go through after the winter into the Champions League or Europa League.

‘That gives the experience to the young Scottish players and in the end, we’d get the benefit.

‘That’s what I’m looking at more in Scottish football rather than the clubs and the style of play of clubs, that kind of thing.

‘It’s not easy because if you look at the Scottish competition, there’s not many young lads who are getting an opportunity to shine compared to Belgium, France, Germany.’

The specific issue of a lack of opportunities being afforded to players who are eligible for the Scotland under 21 side was highlighted at the recent summit at St Andrews which all 42 clubs attended.

With Turkey the only nation which currently gives fewer minutes, the SFA’s chief football officer Craig Mulholland has tabled two proposals which would see clubs obliged to offer more chances to emerging talents in both league and cup matches.

Optimistic that such changes to the rules would lead to a brighter picture further down the line, Pocognoli added: ‘Hopefully, we can see the benefits in future.

‘I follow all of the young lads, not only from the Premiership in Scotland, but also the Championship and League One because some of them are on loan.

‘My job is not only to win the next game, it’s also to prepare for what’s coming next season.

‘In one year, a lot can change. I try to support all the decisions of the clubs in Scotland regarding the fact they play Scottish players and young ones especially.

‘Colby Donovan is a good example, he played some good games for Celtic and I tried to help to accelerate his progress, then he signed a new contract and plays week after week.

‘He is not selected this time, but I think we will get the benefit later on.

‘For Findlay Curtis it’s the same, he’s not playing a lot at Rangers but I believe in his quality.

‘We need to support those type of players because we need them, but hopefully it can help his pathway at Rangers to get some minutes.

‘I hope some other players will be on the same pathway this season.’

#1611. Michael Olise: Bayern Munich's £265m valuation revealed amid Real Madrid links

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 12:06, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 17:13

Bayern Munich have reportedly placed an extraordinary valuation on Michael Olise as they look to discourage Real Madrid and other European heavyweights from pursuing the former Crystal Palace winger.

According to Spanish publication AS, the Bundesliga champions now value the France international at a staggering €300m (£265m), despite remaining determined to secure his long-term future at the Allianz Arena.

The figure would comfortably exceed the current world-record transfer fee of €222m (£198m), which Paris Saint-Germain paid Barcelona for Neymar in 2017.

Olise has attracted attention from several major European clubs since leaving Crystal Palace for Bayern in a €53m (£45m) deal in the summer of 2024, with Real Madrid among his reported admirers.

However, the German giants are in no hurry to entertain offers for their 24-year-old attacker, who remains under contract until June 2029.

The reported valuation is not an official release clause, nor does it indicate that Bayern are actively looking to sell Olise. Instead, it reflects the exceptionally high price that would potentially be required to persuade the club to consider his departure.

Olise has established himself as one of Europe's most productive attacking players since arriving in Germany, and his performances have strengthened Bayern's determination to retain his services.

The Frenchman registered 22 goals and 29 assists across all competitions last season, helping Bayern retain their Bundesliga crown and earning recognition as the league's Player of the Season.

He has continued that form into the 2026-27 campaign, contributing 12 goals and seven assists in 15 club appearances.

His ability to operate from the right flank, cut inside onto his stronger left foot and create opportunities for teammates has made him a central figure in Vincent Kompany's attacking system.

Bayern are consequently keen to reward Olise with an improved contract, despite having more than two-and-a-half years remaining on his current agreement.

The club have reportedly explored extending his deal until 2032, with a substantial salary increase that could place him alongside Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala among Bayern's highest earners.

However, discussions have yet to produce an agreement.

Previous reports have suggested that Olise's representatives want a release clause included in any new Bayern contract, potentially allowing the player greater control over a future move.

A figure of around £170m has been mentioned in connection with that proposed clause, considerably below Bayern's newly reported valuation.

Those demands remain part of the negotiations rather than agreed contractual terms.

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness has publicly played down concerns over the lack of progress, suggesting that the club have sufficient time to reach an agreement.

"The time will come to reach a new agreement. He has two more years on his contract," Hoeness was quoted as saying by AS.

Sporting director Christoph Freund has also insisted that Bayern are under no immediate pressure to extend the Frenchman's deal, praising Olise's development and reaffirming the club's satisfaction with his performances.

The German champions therefore appear determined to negotiate from a position of strength rather than allow speculation over his future to dictate their decisions.

Real Madrid's interest in Olise has been widely reported, with the Spanish giants previously considering the Frenchman as a potential addition to their attacking options.

The former Reading and Crystal Palace player attracted particular attention following his performances against Madrid in the Champions League, further enhancing his reputation among Europe's elite.

However, AS indicates that Real Madrid are not currently involved in active discussions over the player's future, despite the persistent links.

The emergence of Yan Diomande at the Santiago Bernabeu has also changed the composition of Madrid's attack, potentially reducing the urgency of pursuing another expensive wide forward.

Nevertheless, Olise's technical qualities and versatility make him an attractive long-term option for a club accustomed to recruiting leading attacking talent.

Any attempt to secure his signature would now face an enormous financial obstacle.

Bayern's reported €300m valuation represents almost six times the amount they paid Crystal Palace just over two years ago and would establish a new benchmark in the transfer market.

It is also substantially higher than the approximately €200m (£176m) valuation previously discussed in connection with the player's future.

The Bavarian club's position comes at a time when Olise's contractual demands are already attracting attention, with his future previously linked to Bayern's wider wage structure and Kane's status.

There is currently no indication that Madrid are prepared to meet Bayern's valuation, and the Bundesliga champions have not publicly invited bids for their star winger.

With Olise tied to Bayern until 2029, the club can continue pursuing an extension without facing the immediate prospect of losing him for a reduced fee.

For Real Madrid, the reported price reinforces the scale of the challenge involved in convincing Bayern to part with one of their most valuable players ahead of the summer 2027 transfer window.

#1609. Rwanda vs Mali - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 12:40, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 13:17

The top two teams in Group K of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers face off at Stade Amahoro on Tuesday as Rwanda host Mali.

This is the second meeting between the sides in four days, after Mali edged a 3-2 victory in Bamako last Friday.

Rwanda entered the clash at Stade du 26 Mars on a five-match unbeaten run - four of which were wins - and with the chance to move top of their AFCON qualifying group. They appeared set to do so after goals from Jojea Kwizera and Phanuel Kavita, only for a late collapse to result in a 3-2 defeat.

Beyond missing out on a crucial three points, Stephen Constantine’s men squandered the chance to claim their first victory over Mali in five attempts, a result that would have provided a major psychological boost ahead of the rematch in Kigali.

Amavubi will be eager to return to winning ways and avoid leaving their AFCON hopes in the balance ahead of the final round of qualifiers next March.

Victory on Tuesday could move Rwanda six points clear in the race for a place at the 2027 finals, but defeat could see them slip behind Cape Verde, who are now just behind after their win over Liberia.

Tuesday’s hosts are unbeaten at home since October, keeping clean sheets in three of their last four matches. Another solid defensive display - having never kept a shutout against Mali - would be a key step toward ending their winless run in this fixture.

Like Rwanda, Mali are also in the early stages of a new managerial era, and Anthony da Silva has made an impressive start at the helm - going unbeaten in his first four matches since taking over in June following Tom Saintfiet’s departure.

The most recent of those came against Rwanda last time out, as Les Aigles demonstrated their ability to win matches in different ways by securing their first comeback victory since eliminating 10-man Tunisia at the most recent Africa Cup of Nations.

One of only four teams still boasting a perfect record in the current qualifiers, Mali can move within touching distance of a place at the 2027 AFCON finals, where they will look to extend their run of 10 consecutive tournament appearances dating back to 2008.

Much of that success is due to Mali’s impressive qualifying record, having won five straight and gone 11 matches unbeaten since June 2023 (W9, D2) - a run bettered only by Morocco on the continent in that span.

Not since November 2021 have Tuesday’s visitors won four straight competitive matches, handing them the opportunity to make more history under a manager who has wasted no time stamping his authority on proceedings.

Rwanda Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mali Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Jojea Kwizera was directly involved in both of Rwanda’s goals last time out, and the 27-year-old will be eager to make an impact once again.

Djihad Bizimana has featured in all of his side’s AFCON qualifiers since November 2019 - a streak set to continue on Tuesday.

Ousmane Camara was forced off with an injury late in Mali’s last outing, making the centre-back a doubt for this fixture.

If Camara is unavailable, Cheick Keita could be handed his first competitive start at the heart of the defence.

Lassine Sinayoko has registered five goals and five assists in his last ten appearances for club and country. The Paris FC forward, who set up Moussa Kounfolo Yeo’s equaliser in Bamako, will be aiming to get back on the scoresheet.

Diarra; Traore, Camara, Gassama, Guindo; Sangare, Haidara; Yeo, Doumbia, Nene; Sinayoko

As with last week’s encounter, there is little to separate the sides, so another tightly contested match is expected.

Mali’s superior quality proved decisive in the reverse fixture, but we expect Rwanda to claim a point this time and avoid falling six points adrift of their visitors.

#1608. 'He always wanted to play for Scotland'. Alex McLeish recalls the moment the national team found their new talisman in Scott McTominay

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 11 November 2026

While Alex McLeish’s second stint as Scotland manager clearly did not go to plan, the compensations from that period proved to be significant for the national team.

Without a struggling side earning a play-off spot in the Nations League, a famous night in Serbia under Steve Clarke would never have been possible.

For all we know, the years in international exile may have rolled on. The ongoing improvement which led to participation at the World Cup this summer might never have happened.

McLeish’s greatest legacy, however, was surely to persuade Scott McTominay to pull on a dark blue shirt after he travelled to Carrington in 2018.

Alerted to the Lancaster-born player’s eligibility by then Manchester United manager Jose Mourinho, the man who won 77 caps for his country could have been forgiven for feeling that the coup he pulled off was just never meant to be.

‘The beast from the east,’ McLeish recalled with a grin.

Scott McTominay (left) and Alex McLeish in 2018 ahead of a friendly against Belgium

McLeish and McTominay together in a Nations League encounter against Albania in 2018

‘When I was forced off the train in Newcastle, they said “it’s not going any further, the weather’s knackered.”

‘So, I had to wait for a train down south. And I thought “at this point will I go home?”

‘And I thought, “no, I’ve come this far, so I’m going all the way”. Then I got to my hotel at five in the morning, the guy says, “oh, I thought you were a no-show, son.”

‘I said - “no - I’ve arrived and I’m needing a room.”

‘I didn’t go in for the breakfast as Mourinho said “just come in at lunchtime, get some food and we’ll have a chat.”

‘But he said he (McTominay) definitely wants to play for Scotland.

‘So, it was good to hear that from Jose.’

Mourinho liked what he saw the minute he set eyes on the player. It’s fair to say that not everyone at the club around that time was similarly enthused.

‘He was still just a kid, quite raw,’ McLeish recalled. ‘But he had the physique, speed and skill on the ball.

‘He was good in the air and also with the ball at his feet. It made it a no-brainer.

‘I’d gone to a couple of Man United games and they were just kind of breeding him into the system.

McTominay in training ahead of the Nations League clash against North Macedonia on Friday

‘Listen, anyone would have done it and brought him into the squad.

‘The only problem we faced was that England were in the frame as well. But when I said to Scott, “I’d love you to play for Scotland,” he said “That’s the only team I want to play for.”

‘And all of a sudden we had a brand new young superstar.’

Truth be told, it would be some time before Scotland supporters began to place McTominay in such a bracket.

He had his moments early on for his country, but his deployment as a defender – by both McLeish and Clarke – did him no favours.

It was only in the qualifiers to Euro 2024 that the futility of that approach was accepted.

McTominay was outstanding as a central midfielder in the qualifiers, his performance and two goals in the famous win against Spain topping the lot.

In little over a year, he’d be a Napoli player. And within a season, he’d become a Serie A winner and voted Italy’s best player.

Many Manchester United fans were outraged that the club had sold him for just £25.7million.

Even some England supporters voiced their displeasure about the player slipping through their hands.

‘They have such a massive pot to pick from in England,’ McLeish reflected.

‘But I’m sure that privately, in some of their chats behind the scenes, they will have said ‘we should have got McTominay.’

‘But he chose Scotland. He wanted to to come. He wasn’t saying anything about England at all.

‘And that was the best news I could have got in that era of rebuild.’

While Clarke rightly got the plaudits for taking the team to three tournaments, McLeish has taken a huge amount of pride from the part McTominay has played in it all.

‘It’s incredible how he’s grown and grown,’ he added.

‘In the first few games, he was just trying to feel his way into the international scene. But he gave everything from that first call-up.

Scott McTominay in action against Haiti in the 2026 World Cup

‘He’s played in just about every position in the team down the years. He was in the back four at one stage.

‘But he’s mainly operated in the middle of the field and he’s a real threat in the box and moving from middle to front.

‘The way he runs with the ball is just superb because he really knows what he’s doing.

‘He’s got massive confidence and I hope that a lot of young Scottish players coming into the game can take inspiration from what Scott has done.'

In a rare media conference this week, McTominay put his underwhelming displays at the World Cup in context.

Two days before the opener against Haiti in Boston, he underwent a controlled electric shock in hospital to restore a normal heart rhythm. Since then, he’s undergone a medical procedure to deal with the arrhythmia.

He returns to the Scotland squad a month after pulling on a Napoli shirt again against Frosinone.

With five goals in his past six matches, it feels like the player the Tartan Army grew to love is back with them.

Sebastien Pocognoli may soon feel he owes McLeish a word of thanks, too.

‘It’ll be a massive relief for the manager to get Scott back into the squad,’ he said.

‘You always want your best players available.

‘I remember back in my day, going to Kazakhstan when we had a lot of boys missing.

‘We were held in a bit of limbo. So, for Sebastien to get players into his team of that level will be massive for him. It could make a huge difference for Scotland.’

#1606. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Pascal Gross pulling the strings. 🔎 @Microsoft pic.twitter.com/DAgVsG2B3W

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Like Everton, Newcastle labour to a home win which should have been more comfortable. It would have been had Wissa scored his penalty, but it was a nervy finish as Hull pushed for an equaliser after Cho’s goal.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. There is going to be plenty said about Thierno Barry’s second goal being chalked out because, when you see it, you will wonder what it was for. These are the situations with which I struggle most - if players do not appeal for a wrongdoing, if they don’t feel they have been the victims of an injustice, why are officials getting involved?

Thierno Barry thought he had made it two for Everton, but the goal has been ruled out because Brennan Johnson was judged to be interfering with play and offside. You’re never getting those this weekend after the Enzo Fernandez incident.

Arsenal undone from a corner, swung to the back post and Chema Andres rose above everyone to head home.

This is a remarkable performance by Brighton, who have battered and bullied the champions from the start. Three-nil, and they have even beaten Arsenal at their own game by scoring a set-piece.

I am struggling to remember the last time Arsenal were overrun and outplayed as comprehensively as this. It’s a thrashing.

No half-time subs from Mikel Arteta, which is a little surprising given Arsenal’s predicament.

Brighton have the lead at the Amex and it’s their captain, Pascal Gross, who has provided it. Superb long-range effort, in off the near post. On the overall balance of play, Brighton deserve that. It’s reward for their courage and willingness to go after Arsenal, rather than sitting back.

It took almost 20 minutes but Arsenal have found their feet in this game now. They are starting to find avenues through Brighton’s aggressive pressing and have made a few promising runs in behind, through Havertz and Saka. This is a high quality match.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning important tackles.

The German was incensed by the lack of physicality and intensity in the heavy defeat to Leeds on Monday but the first goal for Joe Wilock came when Lewis Miley won a tackle on the edge of the Hull penalty box.

The second came when Sven Botman came away with the ball just inside his own half. On both occasions Harvey Barnes provided the assist. A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

#1605. Spain vs. England: Three Lions must "worship" Nations League like Cristiano Ronaldo (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 13:26

Former England striker Darren Bent, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has urged the Three Lions to follow Cristiano Ronaldo's example as they prepare to face Spain in their final UEFA Nations League group-stage fixture.

Thomas Tuchel's men take on the world and European champions in Madrid having already sealed a top-two finish in League A Group 3, guaranteeing progression to the quarter-finals.

Victory for England at the Metropolitano Stadium will also assure the Three Lions of top spot in the group, although a draw or defeat will consign them to a second-placed finish.

Nevertheless, England will compete in the Nations League knockouts for the first time since the 2018-19 edition, as they bid to become just the fourth winners of the tournament after Spain, Portugal and France.

While the Nations League is not held in as high regard as the World Cup or Euros, Bent cannot understand supporters who dismiss the competition as glorified friendlies and points to Ronaldo's passion as an example to follow.

Asked by Sports Mole via MrQ sportsbook how big a chance England have of winning the Nations League if they beat Spain, Bent replied: "Massive chance.

"This is my point: I never understand why certain sections of the fanbase turn their nose up at the Nations League when there's a chance to win a trophy.

"I'd love to win the Euros or the World Cup, but it's incredibly hard to do so. You have to develop a winning mentality and culture throughout your nation.

"If you win the Nations League, look at the pride of Cristiano Ronaldo, someone who has won absolutely everything other than the World Cup, takes in winning every trophy. He worships the Nations League because it's an opportunity for his nation to win something.

"If we can win the Nations League and beat Spain and France along the way, I think that's a massive step forward in terms of where we are as a nation. It would show that we can upset the so-called bigger nations in major competitions.

"It's massive for England to go into that game and beat Spain. They're world champions and European champions. To beat them in the Nations League and go on to win the competition would be huge."

Cristiano at FT. ?? https://t.co/ta6iHtds1R

Ronaldo spearheaded Portugal to two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025, and the five-time Ballon d'Or winner was visibly emotional after the Selecao won the most recent edition.

Ronaldo dropped to his knees as Portugal clinched the crown with victory over Spain on penalties, and he admitted after the game that he could not hold back the waterworks.

"Winning for Portugal is always special. I have many titles with clubs, but nothing is better than winning for Portugal. It's tears. It's duty done and a lot of joy," Ronaldo told SportTV last year.

The 41-year-old may no longer be gracing the international stage with his presence, but England players and fans would do well to heed his words when the Nations League knockouts commence.
