Big chance missed from Haaland of all people to make it 4-2 to City in what has been a pulsating, spell-binding first 45 minutes. It’s fast, furious and a helluva lot of fun to watch. Brilliant from Ndiaye to tee up Haaland who shoots wide of a post. A game for attackers shall we say ...

There are significant advantages to having a goalkeeper who is 6ft 5in with long arms and massive hands. Brobbey’s shot cannons off Guehi and would have looped over a number of goalkeeper but Donnarumma sticks out a giant arm to help nudge the ball over the bar and keep City 3-2 in front in the fifth minute of first half stoppages

Not a pretty half from the returning Iraola’s side, who will need to be much better in the second period to challenge for the three points.

Bournemouth have dropped points late on in a number of matches this season and will perhaps rue not being able to capitalise on their early advantage.

City are in front. Again. Semenyo this time, he fires the ball beyond Roefs having collected a loose ball int he box.

Antoine Semenyo gets his first goal of the season! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/1n2W5Cyxz0

A relatively slick Liverpool move sees the ball worked out to Araujo on the right who has minded to bomb on with increasing frequency, and while he’s able to win a corner, Szoboszlai’s delivery is cleared with a minimum of fuss.

Iraola came into this game saying that his side held an advantage having played two days earlier than Bournemouth in midweek. You would never have guessed it from what we have witnessed here today.

And right on cue, a frustrated Isak attempts a specultative effort from range which sails high and wide.

Sunderland are level again as Brobbey scores after lengthy VAR check for offside.

Sunderland fans sing “F--- VAR” and City fans boo the delay while they both awaited the verdict, which has now gone Sunderland’s way

Brian Brobbey levels it AGAIN! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/YvelzwnmY8

Can’t hold a lead today City. Wow, Sunderland are level again in an instant and it’s that man Brobbey again. There’s a VAR check going on to check for offside

So, this is not a rush to make a sweeping criticism, it’s simply an observation. But Liverpool fans will be looking at Bradley Barcola and  waiting to see that first burst, that moment of electricity, that has showed why they bought him. It’s like you look for a touch, a pass, a moment of skill. He’s just had a shot saved but it all seems very tentative for him at the moment. And that is what he needs - a moment.

Jacquet does brilliantly to close down Christie as the Scot was stealing into the box and looking to pull the trigger.

Chances! Barcola forces Petrovic into an awkward-looking save, before follow-up efforts from Wirtz and Gakpo are charged down.

Mac Allister is fouled 25 yards out moments later and Szoboszlai gets another go. Here, he drags his effort just wide.

It’s all happening at the Etihad. Cherki restores City’s lead with his third Premier League goal of the season.

It’s a great finish from Cherki to put City back in front but it doesn’t happen if Ndiaye is quick to read Danso’s risky pass and win possession. Sharp as a button in that moment.

Rayan Cherki puts Manchester City back in front! 💫 pic.twitter.com/PP4MAV9kw3

A really poor piece of defending from Kerkez gives Bournemouth a free-kick out on the right. Tavernier spins in an inswinger but Van Dijk heads clear. Truffert launches another assault on Liverpool’s box off the second phase but Alisson is wise to it and gathers.

It appears that Liverpool are beginning to settle, they take the opportunity to circulate the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure, waiting for the right moment to pounce. The final pass is poor, though, and Araujo through-pass goes all the way through to Petrovic. It was aimed at Isak ...I think.

Some signs of life from Liverpool, as they create a substantial overload down their left, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Barcola and Isak meeting on that flank. Barcola attempts a sprint into the channel off the shoulder of the ball-side centre-back but he is deemed offside. Looked close, but a bit better from Liverpool.

Araujo has the chance to launch a long throw into the box but Silva beats Van Dijk to the summit and Petrovic gathers the loose ball.

Scott then sprays a wonderful ball over to Rayan on the right but his cutback to Tavernier comes to nothing after the midfielder loses the ball. Liverpool then spring a counter of their own, but Bournemouth recover and charge down a hopeful Gakpo effort from the edge of the box.

Liverpool will not be pleased with their start to this match. They’ve struggled to string more than three passes together without ceding possession and Isak has cut an isolated figure up top.

First time that Bournemouth have gone through the gears and the move ends with Alisson Becker saving brilliantly from Evanilson. It’s a funny stadium, here, as it can be quiet then all of a sudden a tempest whips up and you can sense the mood changing. Liverpool are struggling for alacrity and Andoni Iraola is keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz, who is moving gingerly after taking a bang to his left foot.

Some start at the Etihad. You had to wonder if a big early missed chance from Nilson Angulo was going to haunt Sunderland with City taking the lead just a few minutes later through a quite sublime free-kick from Enzo Fernandez. But Sunderland have immediately hit back. Maresca will decry the defending but it’s brilliant from Enzo Le Fee, who surges forward and then splits Nunes and Dias with an inch perfect pass that Brobbey takes beautifully in his stride before finishing.

On Fernandez’s free-kick before then, he’d very much shaped as if he’s going to cross the ball from a free-kick on the right side of the penalty area. He’d clearly spotted an opening in the top right though and, while giving the firm impression to Roefs he was going to whip in a cross, he obviously had other ideas. The execution was immaculate but it was telling just how effectively he’d managed to deceive the Sunderland goalkeeper. It was world class

A slight mix-up sees Kerkez and Wirtz bump into each other by the touchline. The Germany international limps away and grimaces but should be fine to continue.

Chance! Alisson makes amends with a stunning save. Tavernier had hit the by-line and lasered a cross to Evanilson who, with the ball slightly behind him, improvised and flicked it toward the near post. Alisson gets down swiftly and turns behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Jacquet gives away a needless foul on the near side but Scott’s delivery goes straight into Alisson’s hands. The Brazilian’s throw out is poor, though, and Scott darts into Liverpool’s box, just unable to pick out a team-mate.

Barcola is presented with green grass to run into, but just as he builds a head of steam Hill comes across in a flash and snuffs out the foray forward.

Woah, Brobbey responds immediately, stealing in between City defenders before slotting past Donnarumma.

Instant response from Sunderland as Brian Brobbey equalises! 💥 pic.twitter.com/et6AHGPAbl

Enzo Fernandez opens the scoring at the Etihad with a direct free-kick from out wide. Really poor from Roefs who was caught napping. That’s Fernandez’s first City goal.

Enzo Fernandez gets his first Manchester City goal in style! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/fVOnJvACYY

Wirtz earns a free-kick just outside the D. Bournemouth feel aggrieved as there looked to have been an earlier foul on Scott and to make matters worse Szoboszlai is standing over the ball.

His effort leaves Petrovic rooted to the spot but the ball veers just wide of the mark.

Evanilson’s willingness to drop deep is asking questions of Liverpool’s centre-backs. Do they follow him and risk disrupting their backline coverage?

The hosts attempt to work a short corner routine but Truffert’s eventual through-ball is too strong and the ball rolls out for a Liverpool goal-kick.

This wouldn’t go down as a fixture you would circle for being noteworthy but make no mistake this is a huge afternoon for Liverpool. They have had some days at the Vitality Stadium in recent years and last season’s defeat put a huge dent in Arne Slot’s hopes of trying to find a revival. It’s also a big test for Bournemouth, coming down from the euphoria of beating Real Sociedad. Let’s see how it all transpires.

Evanilson makes a smart run into the right channel and while Jacquet gets his foot on the ball he’s instantly smothered by Scott and the ball goes out for a Liverpool goal-kick. A sign of how high both sides will be willing to jump in search of the ball.

Both sides will look to force mistakes out of the other and Szoboszlai is able to pick Adams’ pocket on the halfway line. He offloads to Araujo who runs into a cul de sac down the right flank.

We are under way at the Vitality. Bournemouth are in their customary black-and-red home shirts kicking from right to left and Liverpool are in their white away kit and red shorts.

The players have emerged from the tunnel, Van Dijk and Smith at the front of the lines. A few pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere but one thing missing is the accidental sitting in the wrong dugout from the returning Iraola. He knows where he’s going.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”

Your Eagles at Elland Road 🦅 pic.twitter.com/QGBqKJoSD1

Bournemouth signed Truffert from Rennes in the summer of 2025 to replace Kerkez – who had just joined Liverpool – and the left-back has been a revelation at the Vitality. So much so that this week he earned himself a call-up to Zinedine Zidane’s first France squad.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#1567. Everton targeting Iceland international as Thierno Barry alternative

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.

David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

Real Sociedad striker Orri Oskarsson is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, with Everton understood to be paying particularly close attention to his progress.

The 22-year-old has impressed in Spain, and the Toffees could explore a move as they look to address a key weakness in their squad.

According to TEAMtalk, Everton are among the clubs monitoring Oskarsson ahead of the January transfer window. Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Brentford are also reportedly tracking the Icelandic forward, meaning Moyes could face competition if Everton decide to pursue a deal.

Everton’s need for a striker has become increasingly apparent following their summer business. Beto departed for Fiorentina without a replacement arriving, leaving Thierno Barry as the club’s only recognised centre-forward. Attempts to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco and Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United also failed to produce a deal.

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

The Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

Oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

However, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

The Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1566. Chelsea targeting Trent Alexander-Arnold as surprise transfer opportunity emerges

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Chelsea could be preparing for a significant change at right-back as the club assess their options ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

With uncertainty surrounding Malo Gusto’s future at Stamford Bridge, the Blues have reportedly identified an unexpected target who could bring considerable experience and creativity to their defence.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold has emerged as a potential option, with former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown suggesting the England international could be tempted by a move to west London if Chelsea decide to make an approach.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea are keeping tabs on Alexander-Arnold as questions continue over his role at Real Madrid. The 28-year-old has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter under Jose Mourinho, with competition for places limiting his opportunities.

Brown revealed that Chelsea are among the clubs monitoring the situation, telling Football Insider: “One name who I have heard in connection with a move to Chelsea is Trent Alexander-Arnold.”

He admitted the potential transfer had initially surprised him, adding: “It came as a bit of a surprise to me, to be honest, but he has fallen well down the pecking order at Real Madrid to the point where he’s now the second or even third choice.”

The former scout also questioned whether the defender currently fits into Mourinho’s plans, explaining:

“It appears Mourinho doesn’t rate him particularly in that right-back position, and he’s not the only one, because he’s been out in the cold for England as well.”

Despite those concerns, Brown believes Alexander-Arnold remains an attractive player because of his technical ability and reputation. Chelsea, meanwhile, have reportedly been assessing potential replacements for Gusto as they consider changes to their defensive options.

Brown added: “Alexander-Arnold is a talented footballer who has a very good skillset, but it is those weaknesses in his game that often raises concerns.”

He also suggested that Chelsea’s interest in high-profile players could make the move possible: “Chelsea, though, will always be keen on the possibility of signing a big-name player; it’s just what they do, so they’ll be keeping an eye on whether he does become available.”

The possibility of a return to Liverpool has also been discussed, but Brown believes Stamford Bridge could become a realistic destination if the defender decides to leave Spain.

“They’ll want to avoid that situation coming up again, as will he I expect, so Chelsea could be where he ends up and he could be tempted if they decide to make a move.”

However, Alexander-Arnold is not currently pushing for an exit. Previous reporting has suggested he wants to fight for his place at Real Madrid, meaning any potential Chelsea move would depend on how his situation develops.

#1565. Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

In his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

#1564. Ukraine vs Georgia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 15 Nov 2026 16:54

Ukraine welcome Georgia to Kosicka futbalova arena on Tuesday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League B Group 2.

The hosts are third in the standings and two points ahead of their bottom-placed visitors, leaving both teams fighting to confirm their survival in League B.

Ukraine got their 2026-27 Nations League campaign underway with an encouraging 1-0 victory over Hungary, with Danylo Sikan scoring the only goal just before half-time.

After following that result up with a 0-0 draw against Georgia, Ukraine have subsequently fallen to three consecutive defeats, losing 3-0 and 1-0 to Northern Ireland and 2-1 to Hungary.

Andrea Maldera's side, as a result, sit third in Nations League B Group 2 with four points from five matches, and with just one game remaining, Ukraine are unable to climb into the promotion playoff places.

However, Ukraine are still fighting to ensure their survival in League B, as they lead visitors Georgia by only two points, meaning defeat on Tuesday would consign Maldera's men to a relegation playoff fixture.

Ukraine will secure their League B status with at least a draw, and they will, therefore, be hoping to replicate or improve upon their 0-0 stalemate with Georgia in the reverse fixture.

Georgia have failed to win any of their five League B matches, recording two draws and suffering three defeats during that time.

Despite boasting the likes of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Georges Mikautadze in attack, Georgia have also failed to find the back of the net in any of their five matches, while they have conceded four times.

Georgia will be hoping to end their goalless streak when they come up against Ukraine, who have conceded more than any other team in the group (six conceded).

However, Georgia's attack has been weakened by the long-term injury to Kvaratskhelia, who scored the nation's last goal in their 2-0 victory over Bahrain in a friendly in June.

Georgia will also have to overcome a miserable record in meetings with Ukraine, having failed to defeat Tuesday's opponents in any of their 12 meetings - losing seven and drawing five.

Ukraine failed to find the net for the third time in Group 2 as they lost 1-0 to Northern Ireland last time out, and Maldera may opt to make changes in attack as a result, meaning the likes of Artem Dovbyk could start.

At the opposite end, captain Mykola Matvienko could start alongside Ilya Zabarnyi, with Illia Krupskyi introduced at right-back.

Meanwhile, Georgia will be without superstar Kvaratskhelia due to a long-term injury, meaning much of the attacking responsibility will rest on Mikautadze's shoulders.

The striker should be supported by Zuriko Davitashvili, Nika Gagnidze and Giorgi Kvernadze, with Anzor Mekvabishvili and Giorgi Chakvetadze in midfield.

Trubin; Krupskyi, Zabarnyi, Matvienko, Mykolenko; Andriyevskiy, Yarmoliuk, Ocheretko, Sudakov; Dovbyk, Krasnopir

Mamardashvili; Kakabadze, Goglichidze, Dvali, Lochoshvili; Chakvetadze, Mekvabishvili; Kvernadze, Gagnidze, Davitashvili; Mikautadze

Georgia have failed to score in any of their five matches and are further weakened by Kvaratskhelia's absence, and with Ukraine boasting the home advantage, we are predicting a win for the hosts.

#1563. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage after disastrous 16-game spell - this is how his reign unravelled over late, intense sessions, dinner at the training ground and an unpopular assistant manager

Published: 10:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:52 EST, 12 November 2026

Crystal Palace have sacked Pierre Sage after players and club chiefs grew frustrated over his training methods, Daily Mail Sport can reveal.

A 3-1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday saw Palace drop to bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years and proved to be the final straw for club bosses.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while the Palace players got on well with the 47-year-old, they were frustrated by his late training sessions – with some not starting until 4pm. The regimented routine required players to stay at the training ground for dinner on the night before matches, with some not returning home until 8pm ahead of a 2pm kick-off the following day.

The club's hierarchy, meanwhile, expressed concerns early in the Frenchman's tenure that he was not doing enough defensive work on the training pitch.

Sage's philosophy was that the best way to defend was having the ball, meaning training sessions focused on running, pressing and possession rather than defensive structure.

But the lack of focus led to a poor defensive record, with Palace conceding 30 goals in 16 matches across all competitions. Defending set-pieces and counter-attacks has been a persistent problem for Sage’s side, and he won just two of his ten Premier League games in charge.

Pierre Sage has been sacked by Crystal Palace after a dismal start to the season saw them win just two of their first ten games

Palace sit rock bottom of the Premier League, their leaky defence having conceded 24 goals

Daily Mail Sport understands many players voiced fears they were being pushed too hard in training, with sessions the day before a game particularly intense. There were also significant concerns about the quality of Sage's backroom staff, with his assistant Jamal Alioui proving especially unpopular among the players.

There has also been considerable turnover among senior executives, with six departures over the past 18 months. Chief financial officer Mitesh Velani is set to add to that number in the coming months. One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that the disruption to the club’s business operations has the hallmarks of a club heading for relegation.

As Palace look to bail themselves out of trouble, Daily Mail Sport understands talks are progressing with former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank, who is expected to take over ahead of crucial games against Coventry and Hull after the international break.

Palace chairman Steve Parish first contemplated sacking Sage over his lack of defensive nous in September, but gave him a stay of execution after Palace kept a clean sheet in a spirited performance away at Leeds on the eve of the international break. However, that display proved an anomaly as Palace shipped 19 goals in the following nine games.

Palace have won just once in their last eight matches in all competitions, beating Fulham 1-0 in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

In September, Daily Mail Sport revealed tensions had emerged between Sage and Parish when the latter took a dim view of the decision to drop teenage defender Jaydee Canvot for their defeat by Ipswich Town.

Palace paid French club RC Lens £4million in compensation to appoint Sage in June after he won the French Cup, finished second in Ligue 1 behind Paris Saint-Germain and was named manager of the season last term. It was the first time in 10 years that Palace had paid compensation to appoint a manager.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (right) first contemplated dismissing Sage in September over a lack of defensive nous

Palace players found Sage’s training sessions too intense and struggled to adapt to the late schedule

Succeeding Oliver Glasner, Palace's greatest manager, proved too big a task for Sage.

Following Palace's loss to Liverpool, Sage insisted the Eagles have been playing better than their league position suggests and pleaded for more time. Those appeals fell on deaf ears.

'A lot of times I’ve said we deserved better and it was the case again (on Sunday),' said Sage. 'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

‘I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in (me), and if it's not the case, they will take a decision. I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100 per cent involved in what I have to do.

‘We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be OK.’

#1562. Manchester United targeting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in surprise January transfer move

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

#1561. England lineup vs. Spain confirmed as Ben White starts in triple change

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 18:34, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 18:46

England and Spain have confirmed their starting lineups for Sunday's UEFA Nations League showdown at the Metropolitano Stadium.

Thomas Tuchel's men must beat the world and European champions to win League A Group 3, although both sides have already sealed their spots in the quarter-finals.

The Three Lions have made three changes for their reunion with La Roja, all of which come in defence, including the already-known switch in goal between James Trafford and Jordan Pickford.

Tuchel has also brought Ben White - who was once again booed by England fans against Croatia on Thursday - back into the starting XI, at the expense of Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Fellow Arsenal man Ezri Konsa is also restored to the starting lineup after missing the midweek victory through injury, taking Dan Burn's place in the heart of defence.

Djed Spence and Myles Lewis-Skelly must make do with spots on the bench following their returns from injury and suspension respectively, as Tuchel sticks with an unchanged midfield and attacking selection.

As for Spain, head coach Luis de la Fuente has made five changes to the side that bested the Czech Republic 2-0 last time out, including expected recalls for Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal.

The pair both missed Spain's penultimate group game as a precautionary measure, but they have unsurprisingly been selected over Yeremy Pino and Ferran Torres this time around.

De la Fuente has also made a bold call in the number 10 role, demoting Fermin Lopez in favour of Mikel Merino, but Alex Baena hold his spot on the left over Nico Williams - now fully fit again following illness.

Merino's Arsenal teammate Martin Zubimendi is also retained in midfield over Pedri, despite concerns over fatigue having played the full 90 against the Czech Republic amid a lack of game time at club level.

De la Fuente has made two changes to his backline foe the final matchday, as Marc Pubill replaces Pedro Porro at right-back, and Aymeric Laporte is in for Dean Huijsen in central defence.

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are currently considered the favourites to secure his signature.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

#1559. Unai Emery's grand plans for Aston Villa after agreeing new contract: Why he believes he can win Champions League, the Pep Guardiola blueprint and changing his mind on selling stars

Published: 07:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:54 EST, 12 November 2026

Aston Villa hope Unai Emery will become their answer to Sir Alex Ferguson but when planning the current stage of his career the Spaniard had another boss in mind.

Having agreed a new contract that will make him one of the two best paid managers in the Premier League, Emery has the sort of structure at Villa that Pep Guardiola enjoyed for a decade at Manchester City.

Emery has always regarded Guardiola as the world’s best coach – and not just for the teams he has produced and the trophies he has won. The Basque admired Guardiola’s refusal to compromise on his vision for a club and has adopted those principles every step of the way at Villa, leading them from the bottom half to the Champions League.

‘We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a (new) deal, yes,’ Emery said last Friday, of a meeting he had with key figures at Villa including co-owner Nassef Sawiris a few days earlier. ‘Nassef is very ambitious, a hard worker and his commitment to the club is huge. It’s easy for me to have meetings with him as normally we are on the same page.’

This season began slowly but after six league games unbeaten, Villa are back in the top half and three points off the top five, as well as sitting sixth in the Champions League group phase with three wins from four.

After Emery underlined his desire to stay at Villa Park, Daily Mail Sport looks at what comes next for him and Villa.

Aston Villa hope Unai Emery will become their answer to Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares to extend his stay in the Midlands

After a slow start this season, Villa are in fine form in both the Premier League and Champions League

With about two-and-a-half years still remaining on Emery’s previous deal, there was no need for Sawiris to rush. His decision is both a show of faith and a recognition of the current climate.

Emery was on a five-man shortlist to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United but Daily Mail Sport understands he is unlikely to have moved to Old Trafford even without the contract discussions.

Studying Guardiola convinced Emery that to be successful, a manager needs control. He cannot operate if he has only limited influence over recruitment, or if he has no say in senior appointments – something United are highly unlikely to have granted.

Unlike at many clubs, where sporting directors and heads of performance are brought in by the chairman or chief executive, Emery has driven the key hires at Villa. Since Emery’s arrival, the number of Spanish backroom staff at Villa has grown well into double figures.

Director of football operations Damian Vidagany moved to Villa with Emery in 2022 and was a key reason why Emery accepted the job. Emery also pushed for Monchi to be brought in as ‘president of football operations’ and when that went wrong, he was allowed to select the next guy – Roberto Olabe. It is hard to imagine many other clubs where that would happen.

So far Olabe has been much better than his predecessor, whose dire record in the market saw him ditched a little more than a year ago.

Emery would have had none of this influence at United. In Sawiris, he has a highly supportive boss – contrast that with Sir Jim Ratcliffe. He makes the final calls on recruitment, rather than relying on the equivalent of Jason Wilcox.

Emery’s sense of self-worth is too great and his record too impressive to accept answering to executives of inferior ability. At Villa, he answers only to the ownership group, and he has forged a rock-solid relationship with Sawiris.

Emery was the driving force behind the appointments of director of football operations Damian Vidagany (left) and president of football operations Roberto Olabe (right)

Emery has a rock-solid relationship with co-owner Nassef Sawiris

There are few top clubs these days where the manager has a direct line to the owner but the Sawiris-Emery connection took shape in the autumn of 2022, weeks before he was hired. Sawiris could see the Steven Gerrard experiment was failing and wanted a top-class manager. He looked at Mauricio Pochettino, Thomas Tuchel and Emery.

After a difficult experience at Arsenal, Emery had won the Europa League with Villarreal and was assured by Sawiris that he would have the run of Villa. Emery felt he had never had this level of influence during his 18 months at Arsenal and throughout the process, Sawiris has been as good as his word.

Emery joined on just under £10million per year and his new salary would be close to double that. His wishes in the market have been backed, even when it has been tricky to make the sums add up. Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio were signed on loan at huge expense in January 2025 to deliver Champions League football. That did not happen, but there was no blowback for Emery because Sawiris trusted the direction of travel.

Every one of his requests has been approved. The current stadium redevelopment was planned for 2024 but was shelved because Emery did not wish to play Champions League games in a three-sided ground. Now, he has accepted the bigger picture.

At the training ground, a 40-room hotel was signed off on Emery’s say-so. When Harvey Elliott was brought in on loan and then left in the cold, or when £26m signing Evann Guessand proved a mistake, it was Monchi who took the rap, not Emery.

That sort of loyalty cuts both ways. With their stock so high, how many managers would have stuck around after six of their first-choice starting XI from a Europa League final win had been sold? Emery is taking a risk to his reputation by leading this rebuild but he trusts both himself and Sawiris to get it right.

Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio were signed on loan at huge expense in 2025 to deliver Champions League football. There was no blowback for Emery when that did not happen

When Harvey Elliott was brought in on loan and then left in the cold, or when £26m signing Evann Guessand proved a mistake, it was Monchi (pictured) who took the rap, not Emery

There was a moment at the end of Friday’s press conference when Emery showed just how much he was invested in Aston Villa.

The Spaniard had just been asked if he could elevate Villa to the same level as Europe’s giants and instead of delivering the usual platitudes, Emery referred to the Deloitte Money League, which ranks clubs by the revenue they generate.

To emphasise his point, Emery grabbed his phone, found the page and confirmed that Villa had risen to 14th in the 2024-25 list, generating £376m in that period.

How many top-flight managers are even aware of the Deloitte Money League, let alone their club’s position in it? When asked about finances, most bosses will – quite legitimately – answer that these matters are for senior executives to handle.

Not Emery, who has made a definite shift in recent seasons. He now understands that because of Villa’s financial needs, part of his job will be to sign promising players, increase their value and then – potentially – sell them for double the fee.

This summer, Villa sold Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Ollie Watkins for a combined £253m. They were signed for a total of just £48m.

You can already picture Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi, two of the summer additions, falling into this category.

The unknown is how Emery might feel about this strategy in two or three years’ time if Villa slip out of contention for the Champions League.

Because for all the justifiable enthusiasm about a new contract, this will not be an easy road. Not surprisingly for an overhauled team, Villa are inconsistent.

Villa bought Morgan Rogers (fourth left), Ollie Watkins (fourth right), Ezri Konsa (right) and Youri Tielemans (not pictured) for a combined £48m, then sold them all this summer for £253m

You can already see Johan Manzambi - signed for £52m this summer - being the next player Villa make a huge profit from

After the Europa League triumph in May, Emery's dream is to win the Champions League and last week he made a strong case for saying he could do so with Villa

Throw in their issues with financial regulations and the stadium rebuild and it would be no shock – nor any disgrace – if they finished outside the top five for the next couple of seasons.

Would that be enough for Emery, though? His dream is to win the Champions League and last week he made a strong case for saying he could do so with Villa.

Emery cited Leicester winning the Premier League and his own journey with Villarreal to the Champions League semi-finals in 2022.

Yet the rules are stacked in favour of the wealthiest and no matter how hard they try, Villa may never crack the code. By investing so heavily in Emery, though, Sawiris believes he is giving them a proper shot.

#1558. CorSport: RedBird could consider stock market listing of Milan’s new holding company

AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment, could be publicly listed within five years according to a report.

Yesterday, RedBird announced the creation of a new holding company for the AC Milan project, named Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE). The main goal is to have everything under one roof, from the football team to the new stadium and the NBA Europe project.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Cardinale himself said, there will be several new revenue streams that ultimately will benefit the football club, making it possible to invest more money in players and additional infrastructure. In short, it’s a big project and it could get even bigger.

Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.

By Joel Lefevre | 15 Nov 2026 19:06

On Tuesday, the USA aim to give their manager a fitting send-off when they host Haiti in the second leg of that quarter-final CONCACAF Nations League tie at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati.

It would require an epic collapse for the Yanks to be eliminated from this tournament on Tuesday, having beaten the Haitians 6-0 in leg one.

For the final time, Mauricio Pochettino will be on the US sidelines Tuesday, hoping to end his tenure on a positive note before heading to Old Trafford to join Manchester United.

While he leaves the national team program without a trophy, the Argentine coach has seen this team flourish since the World Cup concluded, and they are currently on a five-match winning run across all competitions.

Pochettino’s men have been near-flawless since the fall, posting three successive clean sheets while netting three or more goals in four of their last five encounters.

The US have only lost three Nations League knockout matches, boasting a 100% home record in quarter-final outings.

Tuesday will mark their fifth international at TQL Stadium, with the Yanks undefeated at the venue, including two wins.

They are unbeaten in their last 11 internationals against Haiti, winning those last four meetings by a combined margin of 10-1.

David Badia’s men have lost their last two matches by a combined margin of 8-0 after winning their first three Nations League group outings.

The Haitians have not won a quarter-final contest in a CONCACAF competition since the 2019 Gold Cup when they were down 2-0 and stunned Canada 3-2.

They have not lost a League A encounter in this tournament when netting the opening goal since the 2023 group stage when Jamaica beat them 3-2.

Les Grenadiers can claim their first victory over the US on American soil Tuesday since 1969, when they beat them 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier in San Diego.

At 18, Julian Hall was the youngest player in the US starting 11 on Saturday, while Santiago Casteneda and Reed Baker-Whiting are seeking their first senior caps.

Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie both featured for the first time since the World Cup this past weekend, with the former netting a brace and the latter adding one, with Hall, Auston Trusty and Folarin Balogun also scoring.

There are two Haitian players without a cap to their name, including goalkeeper Jonah Mednard and midfielder Miguel Joseph.

Chelsea are continuing to assess their defensive options as they plan for future transfer windows, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon emerging as a player attracting attention.

The 21-year-old has impressed in Italy, and his performances have reportedly placed him on Chelsea’s recruitment radar.

According to the Mail Online, the Blues are keeping track of his development as they consider potential additions to their defence.

Ramon has attracted interest after establishing himself at Como. His performances have reportedly caught the attention of several major clubs, with Chelsea among those monitoring his progress.

However, securing his signature may prove complicated because of Real Madrid’s contractual position. The Spanish giants are understood to have retained buy-back and sell-on clauses when Ramon left the club for Como.

Those provisions could give Madrid considerable influence over the defender’s future and potentially make negotiations more difficult for interested clubs.

Chelsea are also likely to face competition from Arsenal and Manchester United, who have reportedly been linked with the young centre-back.

Ramon represents a potential long-term defensive addition for Chelsea as the club looks to maintain depth and quality at the back.

His development in Serie A makes him an interesting option, but Chelsea would need to navigate Real Madrid’s contractual rights and competition from other Premier League sides.

For now, the reported interest appears to be part of Chelsea’s wider recruitment monitoring rather than evidence of a formal bid or advanced negotiations.

#1554. Liverpool step up pursuit of 21-year-old Russia international amid interest from Barcelona and PSG

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Liverpool continue to assess potential additions to their attacking options as the club looks towards future transfer windows. One name attracting attention is Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, although the Reds could face serious competition from some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

The 21-year-old has made an impressive start to life in Turkey following his summer move from Lokomotiv Moscow.

His performances have reportedly caught Liverpool’s attention, but Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are also keeping tabs on his situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Liverpool and Arsenal have stepped up their interest in Batrakov after sending scouts to watch him during Galatasaray’s 4-2 Champions League victory over Lille. The Russian midfielder found the net in that match, further strengthening his growing reputation.

Liverpool are not alone in monitoring the youngster. Manchester United, Chelsea and Manchester City have also been credited with interest, while Barcelona and PSG remain potential destinations.

Batrakov joined Galatasaray from Lokomotiv Moscow in August for €25million and has quickly made an impact. The attacking midfielder has reportedly contributed goals in European competition, with his technical quality, creativity and ability to threaten the opposition goal making him an attractive prospect.

One of the most significant details surrounding his future is a reported release clause worth around £50million. The clause is understood to allow him to leave Galatasaray for a club in one of Europe’s top four leagues, potentially giving Liverpool a clear route to pursuing a deal.

However, Galatasaray are reportedly pleased with their summer signing and have little desire to sell him so soon after his arrival.

TEAMtalk also reports that Barcelona have monitored Batrakov for some time, while PSG continue to be viewed as a possible destination. Both clubs could offer strong competition if Liverpool decide to turn their scouting interest into a concrete move.

For Liverpool, Batrakov represents a potential opportunity to secure a highly regarded young attacking midfielder with considerable room for development. His creativity and goal threat could make him an interesting option as the club continues to assess its long-term attacking plans.

The reported £50million release clause provides some clarity over the financial side of a possible transfer. Nevertheless, Liverpool would still need to convince the player that Anfield is the right destination, particularly with Barcelona and PSG reportedly capable of appealing to him.

A January move appears less realistic, with Galatasaray having little interest in losing a player they only signed in the summer. A deal next summer could be a more plausible scenario if Liverpool maintain their interest.

For now, the Reds’ reported scouting activity suggests Batrakov is firmly on their radar, but there is no indication that a formal bid has been submitted. Liverpool will need to continue monitoring his progress before deciding whether to pursue the £50million-rated midfielder.

#1553. Mauricio Pochettino should TURN DOWN the Man United job unless he gets TWO new signings to fix 'the worst back four in the Premier League', says Gary Neville

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:19 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 10:08 EST, 12 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino has been warned against taking the Manchester United job, by Gary Neville unless the club's hierarchy promise to back him in the January transfer window and bolster 'the worst back four in the Premier League'.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Pochettino is expected to be named as the new Red Devils head coach, replacing Michael Carrick. Carrick was pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning before being sacked just hours later.

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning too. He had been in Monaco the day before with the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Upon Pochettino's expected arrival, he will join a club languishing in the relegation zone - with United 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 matches.

United have conceded 19 goals across those 10 games - with only 14th-placed Ipswich Town (20) and bottom side Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) has been warned against becoming the new Manchester United head coach by Gary Neville unless they promise him defensive reinforcements in January

Michael Carrick arrives at Carrington on Thursday morning ahead of his Man United sacking

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning after being in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's fate at the club

And speaking about Pochettino's pending arrival, Neville insists on the Argentine making ultimatums to the board if they want him - starting with improving the defence.

'If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven,' he said on The Overlap.

'He'll do that with a pay-off. So do that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January. He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer we're not to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

'They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.'

Expanding further, the former United right back didn't hold back in his criticism of the current defensive options at the club.

'I mean look the back four that he finished with on Sunday was [Diogo] Dalot left back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,' he said.

'That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. That is I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.'

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

Neville believes Manchester United have 'the worst back four in the Premier League'

Diogo Dalot (left) gave away a penalty during United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and Pochettino may even would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.
